info.text: Unit 32 — base check to certified release. Listening, Reading, Use of English, Vocabulary.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. How many task cards are in the work pack?

generalfeedback.text: The shift lead says, “There are forty task cards.” Each card has steps and a sign-off box.

feedback.text: Correct — “There are forty task cards.”
No — that number is not said in the briefing.
No — listen again for the exact count.
No — “fourteen” and “forty” sound close; the answer is forty.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. The service bulletin is mandatory.

generalfeedback.text: The service bulletin is recommended, not mandatory. Only the airworthiness directive is mandatory.

feedback.text: No — the service bulletin is recommended, not mandatory.
Correct — it is recommended; the team plans it if time allows.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 1 again. How many airworthiness directives are due on this visit? Write a number.

generalfeedback.text: “One airworthiness directive is due” — a mandatory check on the rudder fitting.

feedback.text: Correct — exactly one airworthiness directive is due.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. What does the built-in test equipment report on the number two fuel pump?

generalfeedback.text: The BITE reports a low-flow finding. A functional test then confirms the pump is unserviceable.

feedback.text: Correct — the readout shows low flow on the pump.
No — the fault is about flow, not the electrics.
No — the finding is on the fuel pump, not hydraulics.
No — the flow is low, not high.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. A duplicate inspection is required after the fuel-system work.

generalfeedback.text: Yes — “A duplicate inspection is required on critical systems.” A second engineer checks the work.

feedback.text: Correct — the fuel system is critical, so a second check is required.
No — a duplicate inspection is required on the fuel system.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 2 again. For how many days does the minimum equipment list allow one pump as a deferred defect? Write a number.

generalfeedback.text: “The minimum equipment list allows one pump as a deferred defect, but only for three days.”

feedback.text: Correct — three days.

questiontext.text: Listen to Dialogue 3 again. How many cards had a sign-off at the start of the final check?

generalfeedback.text: “Thirty-nine cards have a sign-off. One card is still open” — the fuel pump card.

feedback.text: Correct — thirty-nine were signed; one was still open.
No — all forty were complete only at the very end.
No — listen again for the exact count.
No — that number is not said in the dialogue.

questiontext.text: Listen to the Night-shift handover again. At what time was the certificate of release to service issued? Write it as a 24-hour number, for example 0930.

generalfeedback.text: “The certifying staff issued the certificate of release to service at eighteen hundred” = 1800.

feedback.text: Correct — eighteen hundred is 1800.

questiontext.text: Listen to the Night-shift handover again. At the handover, one defect is still deferred.

generalfeedback.text: No — “Nothing is deferred.” The one finding was rectified and tested.

feedback.text: No — nothing is deferred at the handover.
Correct — nothing is deferred; the finding was rectified.

questiontext.text:
Read this work order line, then answer.

Work Order 7781 — raised to change the number two fuel pump. It links Task Card 28-22-00 and the tech log. It stays open until the sign-off is complete.

When does the work order close?

generalfeedback.text: A work order tracks a job and closes only when the sign-off is complete — not before.

feedback.text: Correct — the line says it stays open until the sign-off is complete.

answer.text: as soon as the old pump is removed from the aircraft

feedback.text: No — removing the pump is only part of the job.

answer.text: when the tech log page is first opened for the day

feedback.text: No — opening the tech log does not close the work order.

answer.text: after the night shift takes over the handover report

feedback.text: No — the handover is later and is not the closing rule.

questiontext.text:
Read this work order line, then answer.

Work Order 7781 — raised to change the number two fuel pump. It links Task Card 28-22-00 and the tech log.

The work order links a task card and the tech log.

generalfeedback.text: Yes — the line says it links Task Card 28-22-00 and the tech log, so the paperwork stays joined up.

feedback.text: Correct — it links the task card and the tech log.
No — read the line again: it links both.

questiontext.text:
Read this BITE readout, then answer.

FUEL PUMP 2 — FLOW LOW — CONFIRM WITH FUNCTIONAL TEST.

What does the readout tell you to do next?

generalfeedback.text: The readout says “confirm with functional test”. You prove the fault with a test before you act.

feedback.text: Correct — confirm the low flow with a functional test.

answer.text: change the pump straight away without any further test

feedback.text: No — you confirm the fault first with a test.

answer.text: defer the defect at once under the minimum equipment list

feedback.text: No — deferral is a later decision, not the next step.

answer.text: sign the certificate of release to service right now

feedback.text: No — you cannot release with an open fault.

questiontext.text:
Read this minimum equipment list entry, then answer.

Item 28-10, fuel pump: one pump may be inoperative for three days (Category C).

The entry allows the pump to be inoperative for ten days.

generalfeedback.text: No — the entry allows three days, not ten. Read the number with its unit carefully.

feedback.text: No — it says three days, not ten.
Correct — the entry allows three days.

questiontext.text:
Read this line, then answer.

AD 2019-11-07 is a check on the rudder fitting. It must be closed on this base check.

Which word best describes the airworthiness directive?

generalfeedback.text: An airworthiness directive is mandatory: the word “must” shows there is no choice.

feedback.text: Correct — “must be closed” means it is mandatory.
No — that describes a service bulletin, not an AD.

answer.text: optional if there is enough time

feedback.text: No — the word “must” removes the choice.
No — an AD is a firm instruction, not advice.

questiontext.text:
Add the missing article. Write one word in the gap.

“______ aircraft is ready for service.”

generalfeedback.text: The release statement needs the article: The aircraft is ready for service.

feedback.text: Correct — do not drop the article.
Correct — do not drop the article.
The word is “the” — the aircraft is ready for service.

questiontext.text:
Complete the passive with the correct past participle. Write one word.

“The functional test was ______ out.”

generalfeedback.text: Passive needs the past participle: the test was carried out — never “was carry out”.

feedback.text: Correct — was carried out.
Use the past participle: carried.

questiontext.text:
Add the correct preposition. Write one word.

“The aircraft is ready ______ service.”

generalfeedback.text: The fixed phrase is ready for service, never “ready to service”.

feedback.text: Correct — ready for service.
The preposition is “for”.

questiontext.text:
Complete the present perfect passive. Write one word.

“The rectification has been ______ out.”

generalfeedback.text: A finished action with a result now: has been carried out.

feedback.text: Correct — has been carried out.
Use the past participle: carried.

questiontext.text:
Write the missing term. One word.

“The signed statement that returns the aircraft to use is the certificate of ______ to service.”

generalfeedback.text: The certificate of release to service (the CRS).

feedback.text: Correct — certificate of release to service.
The word is “release”.

questiontext.text:
Write the missing term. One word.

“A second, independent check of a critical control is a ______ inspection.”

generalfeedback.text: A duplicate inspection — a second engineer checks the critical work.

feedback.text: Correct — a duplicate inspection.
The word is “duplicate”.

questiontext.text:
Choose the correct verb form. Write one word (not “is being”).

“The pump ______ unserviceable.”

generalfeedback.text: A status now uses the present simple: the pump is unserviceable — never “is being unserviceable”.

feedback.text: Correct — the pump is unserviceable.
Use the present simple: is.

questiontext.text: Match each term to its meaning.

generalfeedback.text: These five terms run through the whole event, from the work pack to the release.

answer.text: the full set of task cards and paperwork for one event
a defect found in an inspection and written up for action
the repair that clears a defect
the aircraft book of defects and actions

questiontext.text: Match each term to the verb that goes with it (the collocation).

generalfeedback.text: Learn the verb with the noun: raise a work order, carry out a base check, clear a finding, update the tech log, pass a functional test.

questiontext.text: Match each abbreviation to its full form.

generalfeedback.text: The hangar short forms: AD, SB, MEL, BITE and CRS.

questiontext.text: Match each term to its meaning.

generalfeedback.text: Status and people: serviceable, unserviceable, deferred defect, certifying staff, sign-off.

answer.text: a fault allowed to wait under the minimum equipment list
the licensed person who may sign the release
the dated signature that confirms a step is done
